title: SLA-Aware Scaling Scheduler for Burst-Constrained Dedicated Fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a scheduling layer for the Dedicated autoscaler that explicitly reasons about declared SLA targets (e.g., p99 latency, bounded tail latency, request success rate) while enforcing burst caps per-tenant and fleet-level safety limits. The scheduler will synthesize multiple signals (token throughput, active concurrency, queue depth, recent spike gradients) to produce target scaling actions (add/remove GPU slots, step sizes, and temporary headroom credits). It must integrate with existing runtime admission controls, cost budget constraints, and the fallback model-variant routing policy.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can consume SLO profiles (p50/p95/p99 latency targets and max-queue-depth) and emit scaling decisions in the autoscaling API
Scaling decisions include bounded step size, cooldown, and a safety annotation for why a decision was gated
Simulated burst tests show <= 2x overshoot compared to ideal target and meet p99 latency targets in 90% of runs
Policy respects per-tenant burst caps and global fleet surge fences; no unbounded scale-ups observed during chaos tests
End-to-end e2e tests and rollout steps documented; monitor dashboard shows clear decision provenance (metrics + rule match)
progress: 2026-01-10: Initial triage and scoping with Product. Identified core SLO inputs and required outputs to autoscaler API.
2026-01-15: Prototype scheduler written using a hybrid ruleset + lightweight predictor (exponential spike detector). Early sim shows good tracking on synthetic sinusoidal bursts.
2026-01-21: Design review with Runtime and Platform teams. Decision: keep core algorithm deterministic (no opaque ML loop) to simplify debugging and certification for Dedicated customers.
2026-01-25: Trade-off discussion: aggressive step sizes reduce p99 but increase cost; agreed to implement configurable cost-sensitivity weight and per-tenant budget guardrails.
2026-01-28: Integrated safety limits: per-tenant burst cap enforcement, global surge fence, and a step-decay cooldown. Implemented safety-annotation metadata on each decision for auditability.

2026-01-30: Ran chaos test on a staging dedicated fleet (10 nodes). Observed a transient 30% overshoot unrelated to scheduler logic — root cause: slow node JOIN path in orchestration. Created follow-up ENG ticket.
2026-02-02: PRs opened for autoscaler integration and runtime admission hook; invited Platform for security review and SLO smoke tests next week. Preparing rollout runbook.
notes: Algorithm: prioritized hybrid policy that composes three terms: (1) short-term spike gradient predictor, (2) long-term throughput mismatch integrator, (3) safety penalty for headroom consumption. Output is step recommendation clipped by surge fences.
Simulations: used production-like request traces from Jan/2026 with synthetic 10x bursts to validate stability. Baseline compared to current conservative stepper shows 18% lower p99 during ramp-ups.
Observability: new 'Scaling Decision' event added to telemetry schema (decision_id, rationale_tags, predicted_latency, applied_step). Dashboard tile: /dashboards/dedicated/scaling-decisions
Testing: unit tests for decision logic, scenario runner for replaying traces, and an end-to-end k8s staging job for canarying decisions under controlled failures.
Rollout: 3-stage canary (5% tenants -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if p99 regresses > 10% or cost increases >15% week-over-week. Manual approval for dedicated enterprise tenants.
qa_plan: Replay historical traces with and without synthetic bursts to compare p99 and overshoot metrics
Inject orchestration delays to validate safety fences prevent runaway scale-ups
Run tenant isolation smoke tests to ensure per-tenant burst caps are enforced
Validate telemetry provenance: every autoscaler decision must correlate with a decision event and dashboard entry
release_notes: Introduces SLA-aware scaling scheduler for Dedicated fleets: improved latency adherence during bursts and explicit safety annotations for decisions
Configurable cost-sensitivity and per-tenant burst caps to limit spend during transient events
New telemetry for decision provenance to aid debugging and audits
